name: Teeth whitening before photos

lead: Whitening shortly before photos or an event lightens your teeth for a brighter smile on the day.

Wikipedia reports that in-office treatment may lighten teeth by 2 to 7 shades, while strips, trays and whitening toothpastes typically produce 1 to 2 shades. Methods include dentist-applied peroxide gels, tray-based gels, strips and rinses.

paras: People start strips or trays a week or two ahead or book an in-office session a few days before the event, then keep up with whitening toothpaste. Part of the immediate change may reverse within days.

Tooth and gum sensitivity is common, and gum irritation can occur from gels. Part of the shade change can fade within days, and people with dental restorations or gum disease usually check with a dentist first.

web.title: Home-based whitening of teeth in adults - Cochrane

angle.text: Peroxide whitening timed before a photo shoot or event lightens your teeth for a brighter smile in pictures. The shade change is visible on the day, though part of it can fade over a few days.

lead: Teeth whitening before photos is the practice of brightening teeth shortly before a photo shoot, event or date so the smile looks whiter and more polished in pictures. Methods include dentist-applied peroxide gels, tray-based gels, strips, whitening toothpastes and rinses.[1]

Wikipedia reports that in-office treatment may lighten teeth by 2 to 7 shades, while strips, trays and toothpastes typically produce 1 to 2 shades. Part of the immediate change may reverse within days.[1]

A 2018 Cochrane review of 71 trials in 3,780 adults found that home bleaching agents whitened teeth more than placebo over periods from two weeks to six months; sensitivity and oral irritation were the most common side effects, generally mild and temporary, with low to very low certainty evidence on which method is best.[2]

paras: In-office whitening uses peroxide gels, sometimes with light activation. At-home options include strips, rinses, toothpastes and tray gels.[1] A 2012 meta-analysis found light helps only when used properly, and a 2015 study found no measurable benefit from light activators.[1]

Wikipedia states nearly half of the change from a one-hour in-office treatment may be lost within a week, partly due to tooth dehydration.[1] Results can last several months depending on lifestyle.[1]

Sensitivity is common, reported in 67 to 78 percent of in-office patients in a cited figure, lasting about 4 to 39 days. Peroxide at 10 percent or more can burn soft tissue, and over-bleaching can produce a translucent look. Caution is advised for children under 16, pregnant or breastfeeding people, and those with gum disease or cavities.[1]
The EU limits retail products to 0.1% hydrogen peroxide, allowing up to 6% only under dental supervision for adults. The US FDA endorses gels up to 6% hydrogen peroxide or 16% carbamide peroxide.[1]

Whitening is commonly discussed as an inexpensive appearance step, and timing it before photos is a practice some describe in order to get the brightest result at the event while leaving time for sensitivity to settle and for early rebound. A T Nation thread about looking one's best includes a poster asking which home whitening kit to use for 'super white teeth', and a reply laying out teeth whitening as one of the steps to a better smile [3]. A separate T Nation thread on looking good for an event treats a few weeks of preparation as a standard approach [4].

Reported research includes a 2012 meta-analysis on light activation, a 2018 Cochrane review on home-based whitening and research in young participants showing improved oral-health-related quality of life, reduced by tooth sensitivity.[1]

A 2018 Cochrane review of home-based bleaching found 71 trials (26 against placebo, 51 comparing agents), reporting that agents whitened more than placebo in the short term, that sensitivity and irritation were most frequent with higher concentrations and were mild and temporary, and that evidence was low to very low certainty and could not show which concentration, method or duration is best [2].

lore.intro: Whitening is widely treated as a baseline grooming step in appearance communities.

claims.claim: Whitening shortly before photos gives an immediately brighter smile.
A few weeks of home whitening is enough to get a noticeably brighter smile for an event.

timeline.event: Haywood and Heymann publish support for custom-tray carbamide peroxide bleaching.[1]
